clue.text: Pine in Florida for a highball, say, with ice

parts.note: a lob is a ball hit or thrown high, so a highball is an example of one
an ice lolly, often just called a lolly in Britain, is a frozen sweet on a stick

explanation.surface: Someone in Florida reaches for a highball cocktail on the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like longing, and 'highball' like a drink; both mislead. A LOLLY is the British name for an ice lolly, a frozen treat on a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: The loblolly is a pine tree native to the southern United States, including Florida.

clue.text: Landowners bringing atmosphere into SLD assembly

indicators.note: into means the atmosphere word goes inside the other letters
an assembly of letters can be put together in any order

parts.note: air is atmosphere

explanation.surface: Landowners bring their atmosphere into a meeting of the Social and Liberal Democrats.
explanation.walkthrough: The SLD were the Social and Liberal Democrats, a British party of the late 1980s. 'Assembly' rearranges SLD into LDS, which takes in AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Lairds are landed proprietors in Scotland, owners of estates.

clue.text: Plight of girl and boy hill-climbing in the interior

indicators.note: in the interior means the hill goes inside the pair of names

parts.note: Beth is a girl's name

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads the hill upwards, so it is reversed

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill
Al is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl and boy face a predicament while hillwalking inland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plight' looks like a predicament but is the old noun for a pledge, as in plighting one's troth. 'Climbing' turns the hill upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To plight one's troth is to pledge to marry, so a plight is an engagement.

clue.text: Deliveries a couple of students made covering everything

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries
L is the learner sign, so two learners give LL

explanation.surface: A pair of students bowl a set of deliveries between them.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER is a set of six balls bowled in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall means taking everything into account, all-inclusive.

clue.text: A walk set up this beast of burden

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the words are read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a mall is a sheltered walk or promenade, like the Mall in London

explanation.surface: A path is laid out for a pack animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American pack animal, used for carrying loads.

clue.text: Riot caused by aristocratic bishops in revolutionary centre

indicators.note: in tells us the aristocratic and bishops letters sit inside the centre piece

parts.note: a hub is the centre of a wheel, the point round which it revolves
U is the old label for upper-class usage, as in 'U and non-U'
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Unrest erupts when blue-blooded churchmen are caught at the heart of a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests rebels, but here it means turning round: a wheel revolves about its hub.
explanation.definitionFit: A hubbub is a noisy uproar or commotion, much like a riot.

clue.text: Clever point peacekeepers accepted untouched

indicators.note: accepted means the peacekeepers take the other letters inside them

parts.note: UN peacekeeping forces come from the United Nations
neat means clever or skilful, as in a neat trick
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A smart argument is taken on board by a peacekeeping force without being touched.
explanation.definitionFit: Food left uneaten has not been touched, left on the plate.

clue.text: Capability our railways possess?

parts.note: BR was British Rail, the national railway of Britain
to own is to possess

explanation.surface: Asking whether our trains have what it takes.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancelot 'Capability' Brown was a famous English landscape gardener; BR, British Rail, ran Britain's railways.
explanation.definitionFit: The 18th-century landscape gardener Lancelot Brown was nicknamed Capability, so the nickname leads to his surname.

clue.text: In the grip of drink, bearer is acting disloyally

definitions.note: a phrase describing what a person does; the answer is the person doing it

indicators.note: in the grip of means the drink holds the bearer inside it

parts.note: beer is a drink
a tray bears or carries things

explanation.surface: A drunken waiter turns traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearer' looks like a person carrying something, but it is a tray. The definition describes the person, with 'is' linking: one acting disloyally.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitor is someone acting disloyally toward those who trusted them.

clue.text: A Titan held it up after noon in a vanished continent

indicators.note: held means the Titan's name grips the other letters inside it

parts.note: Atlas was the Titan who held up the heavens

indicators.note: after means the reversed it comes after noon
in a down clue up means the word is read upwards, reversed

explanation.surface: A giant of myth held something aloft after midday in a lost land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held it up' reads like the Titan carrying the sky, but it splits: 'held' is the container and 'it up' is the word reversed in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlantis is the legendary island continent said to have sunk beneath the sea.

clue.text: Where we holidayed most recently, all else having failed?

definitions.meaning: read literally, the phrase is the most recent holiday resort visited
the idiom for a final fallback, used when every other option has been tried

explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally the phrase names the latest seaside resort visited; as an idiom it means as a final option when nothing else has worked.

clue.text: 3-D scene in stage show about: cow girl

indicators.note: about means the stage show letters go around the cow girl

parts.note: a drama is a play put on the stage
in Greek myth Io was a maiden turned into a heifer by Zeus

explanation.surface: A three-dimensional set appears in a theatre production involving a cowgirl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow girl' suggests a rodeo performer, but it is Io from Greek myth, a girl turned into a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional model scene, often displayed in a museum case.

clue.text: Aerial provided for a girl returning without books

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the a-plus-girl letters wrap around the books
returning means the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A radio aerial has been provided for a girl coming home without any reading matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here, not lacking, and 'returning' turns the girl's name round. 'Provided for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerial and an antenna are the same thing: a rod or wire that picks up radio signals.

clue.text: Quarry gave slip to chap with kilt

indicators.note: giving something the slip suggests dodging it, so the letters wriggle loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A man in a kilt manages to escape his pursuer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarry' looks like the hunted man escaping, but it is the pit. The letters of CHAP and KILT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalk pit is a quarry from which chalk is dug.

clue.text: Eden Park, where animals are kept?

definitions.meaning: the garden of Genesis, a heavenly place
the old sense from Persian of an enclosed park or game reserve

explanation.definitionFit: The garden of Eden is the biblical heaven on earth, and the word first meant an enclosed Persian hunting park stocked with game.

clue.text: Head right away from sheet of rock

indicators.note: away tells us the right letter is taken off the word for head

parts.note: napper is old British slang for the head

explanation.surface: Someone takes their head right away from a rock face.
explanation.walkthrough: NAPPER is dated British slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology a nappe is a large sheet of rock pushed over younger strata.

clue.text: Periodical row when the joke's over

definitions.note: names the moment rather than the thing; the answer is the line delivered at that point

parts.note: Punch was a famous British humorous magazine
a line is a row

explanation.surface: A magazine quarrel breaks out once the fun is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but is a line. Punch was a long-running British humour magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A punchline is the final phrase that delivers the laugh and brings a joke to its end.

clue.text: Criminal investigators' insert has a note missing

definitions.note: a plural possessive naming a body of detectives; the answer is the organisation itself

indicators.note: missing means the a and note letters drop out of the insert word

parts.note: to interpolate is to insert something into a text
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A detective agency's inserted passage is missing a musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: TE (often spelt ti) is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale.
explanation.definitionFit: The international police organisation coordinates crime investigation between countries.

clue.text: Fabric stocked by many London hosiers

indicators.note: stocked by suggests something held within, so the letters sit inside the words many London

explanation.surface: A material is sold by numerous hosiery shops in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fabric, famously used for stockings.

clue.text: Late run designed to be impartial

indicators.note: designed suggests deliberately reshaped, so the letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A late run was arranged to be fair to all sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Neutral means taking no side, unbiased.

clue.text: Lease accommodating border inhabitant

indicators.note: accommodating means the lease word houses the border word within it

parts.note: to rent something is to lease it
a side is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A lease takes in a border dweller.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident is a person living in a place, an inhabitant.

clue.text: Law Lord upset fat dunce

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: lud, as in m'lud, is how a judge is addressed in a British court
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A senior judge is upset by a stout fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'M'lud' (my lord) is the British courtroom address to a judge, so LUD is a lord of the law.
explanation.definitionFit: A dullard is a slow-witted person, a dunce.

clue.text: Outspoken leader of some old conquerors

parts.note: frank means outspoken, candid

indicators.note: leader of means take the first letter of the word some

explanation.surface: A blunt-speaking chief of an ancient invading force.
explanation.definitionFit: The Franks were a Germanic people who conquered Gaul in the early Middle Ages.

clue.text: Set forth with former American poet

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
Ezra Pound was an American poet

explanation.surface: A one-time American poet sets out his ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound is to set forth or explain in detail.

clue.text: Supporters useful to actors

definitions.meaning: beams or posts that hold something up

explanation.definitionFit: Props are both supports holding something up and the theatrical properties handled on stage.

clue.text: Racecourse cheat? More like a Celt!

definitions.meaning: someone who fails to pay a debt on a bet at the races
a comic comparative of Welsh, meaning more Welsh, the Welsh being a Celtic people

explanation.definitionFit: A welsher is someone who reneges on a bet; jokingly, the word is also the comparative of Welsh, more like a Celtic Welshman.

clue.text: Listener's entitlement to produce a script?

indicators.note: a listener only hears the word, so its sound stands in for the spelling

parts.note: a right is an entitlement

explanation.surface: Does a radio listener have the right to compose a script?
explanation.definitionFit: To write is to compose or put words on paper, as in producing a script.

clue.text: Delay for King Charles having arrived in a military depot

parts.note: pro means for, as in pros and cons
CR stands for Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles

indicators.note: in tells us the arrived word goes inside the military depot

parts.note: a station is a military post or base
in means arrived, as when a train is in

explanation.surface: A king's arrival at a military base is held up.
explanation.walkthrough: CR (Carolus Rex) is the Latin royal cipher of King Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: Procrastination is putting things off, which is delay.

clue.text: Endure extremes of 1 ac in the end

parts.note: to last is to endure

indicators.note: extremes of means take only the first and last letters of the answer at 1 across

parts.note: the answer to 1 across, the Florida pine

explanation.surface: Bear the far ends of a clue to the bitter end.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 ac' points to the answer at 1 across; its first and last letters are L and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Lastly means finally, at the close of a list.

clue.text: Outside Leeds, possibly, he's lacking attention

indicators.note: outside means the he's letters sit around the reworked city
possibly signals that the city's letters may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Beyond the city of Leeds, a man is not paying attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leeds' looks like the city in the picture, but 'possibly' makes its letters anagram fodder, wrapped by he's.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedless means careless, paying no heed or attention.
